cm_queen_1.title: Queen Kiss of Death
cm_queen_1.instruction: White to move. Deliver checkmate with the Queen right next to the enemy King.
hints: Look for a square directly adjacent to the black king where the queen is protected by White's king.
cm_queen_1.explanation: The 'Kiss of Death' is the most common mating net: the queen steps right in front of the king, supported by her own king, leaving zero escape squares.

cm_queen_2.title: Queen Corridor Checkmate
cm_queen_2.instruction: White to move. Checkmate the King along the open file.
hints: Cut off the King completely by controlling the fourth rank.
cm_queen_2.explanation: Restricting the king to the edge with coordinated major pieces guarantees swift checkmate.

cm_two_rooks_1.title: The Lawn Mower
cm_two_rooks_1.instruction: White to move. Begin the rolling lawnmower maneuver to restrict Black to the 8th rank.
hints: Alternate rooks rank by rank. Each rook cuts off one line while the other steps forward.
cm_two_rooks_1.explanation: The lawnmower mate rolls the two rooks forward rank by rank, never giving the king a chance to step forward.

cm_rook_1.title: Single Rook Box Mate
cm_rook_1.instruction: Black king must move to the back rank. Find the move that forces Black into the corner.
hints: Waste a tempo with the rook along the 7th rank so Black has to step into opposition!
cm_rook_1.explanation: With King and Rook, you use the king to take the opposition, forcing the defending king to retreat or yield the file.

cm_rook_2.title: Rook Delivering Final Blow
cm_rook_2.instruction: White to move. Checkmate Black trapped on the edge.
hints: Slide the rook all the way to the 8th rank.
cm_rook_2.explanation: When the enemy king is locked on the board edge and blocked by the opposition king, any rook check along the edge is mate.

cm_backrank_1.title: Classic Back-Rank Mate
cm_backrank_1.instruction: White to move. Exploit Black's un-castled pawn wall.
hints: Black's f7, g7, and h7 pawns trap their own king!
cm_backrank_1.explanation: The back-rank mate occurs when a king is trapped behind its own shield of pawns and attacked on the first or eighth rank with no retreat.

cm_backrank_2.title: Back-Rank Deflection
cm_backrank_2.instruction: White to move. Infiltrate the back rank.
hints: Target both the rook and the 8th rank simultaneously.
cm_backrank_2.explanation: Attacking defending pieces while threatening the back rank forces material concessions.

cm_backrank_3.title: Defending Queen Back-Rank Strike
cm_backrank_3.instruction: White to move. Find the dominating queen centralization that suffocates Black's back rank.
hints: Pin down the 8th rank invasion while paralyzing the d8 rook.
cm_backrank_3.explanation: Controlling open files with queen dominance creates unstoppable back-rank checkmate threats.

cm_opera_1.title: Morphy's Opera Mate
cm_opera_1.instruction: White to move. Checkmate using Bishop and Rook coordination.
hints: Eliminate the defending bishop on f8 to clear the back rank for the rook.
cm_opera_1.explanation: Paul Morphy's Opera Box mate uses a bishop to pin and cover escape squares while a rook delivers the coup de grâce.

cm_anastasia_1.title: Anastasia's Mate
cm_anastasia_1.instruction: White's knight controls e7 and g7. Open the file to execute the mate.
hints: The knight locks the escape squares while a rook or queen finishes the job.
cm_anastasia_1.explanation: In Anastasia's mate, a knight seals the escape squares (e7 and g7) while a major piece delivers mate along the file against the edge.

cm_anastasia_2.title: Queen Sacrifice for Anastasia's Mate
cm_anastasia_2.instruction: White to move. Win Black's king defense.
hints: Dismantle the defensive rook first.
cm_anastasia_2.explanation: Removing defenders paves the way for knight-and-rook mating networks.

cm_arabian_1.title: The Arabian Mate
cm_arabian_1.instruction: White to move. Knight on f6 and Rook on the 1st rank. Deliver checkmate in 2 moves.
hints: Bring the rook to the 7th rank threatening Rh7#. Black's only move is to push the h-pawn!
cm_arabian_1.explanation: The Arabian Mate is one of the oldest recorded mating patterns: the knight on f6 protects the rook on h7 while covering the g8 exit square.

cm_arabian_2.title: Arabian Infiltration
cm_arabian_2.instruction: White to move. Drive the king into the corner trap.
hints: Invade with the rook with check.
cm_arabian_2.explanation: Coordinating knight jumps with long-range rook checks drives the king onto the fatal square.

cm_smothered_1.title: Philidor's Legacy (Smothered Mate)
cm_smothered_1.instruction: White to move. Exploit the vulnerable g7 square.
hints: Target g7 directly with queen and knight tandem.
cm_smothered_1.explanation: Smothered mate occurs when a knight checks a king completely boxed in by its own friendly pieces.

cm_smothered_2.title: The Classic Queen Sacrifice Smother
cm_smothered_2.instruction: White to move. Checkmate the King surrounded by his own army!
hints: The knight has nowhere to hide, but it can jump with double check!
cm_smothered_2.explanation: Double check forces the king into the corner, allowing Qg8+ Rxg8, followed by Nf7# smothered mate.

cm_smothered_3.title: Corner Smothered Finish
cm_smothered_3.instruction: White to move. Find the checkmate in 1 move.
hints: Jump the knight to f7!
cm_smothered_3.explanation: Because Black's own rook and pawns prevent the king from moving, Nf7# is instant checkmate.

cm_boden_1.title: Boden's Mate
cm_boden_1.instruction: White to move. The criss-crossing bishop pair controls the board. Find the winning check.
hints: Pin Black's d7 knight before delivering the criss-cross blow.
cm_boden_1.explanation: Boden's Mate occurs when two criss-crossing bishops slice through intersecting diagonals against a castled queenside king.

cm_boden_2.title: Boden's Bishop Strike
cm_boden_2.instruction: White to move. Develop with maximum tactical pressure against Black's king.
hints: Activate the bishop pair quickly.
cm_boden_2.explanation: Developing bishops with active diagonals puts immense pressure on king safety.

cm_double_bishop_1.title: Double Bishop Laser
cm_double_bishop_1.instruction: White to move. Checkmate in 2 moves with the Bishop pair.
hints: Control the escape squares with the first bishop, then strike with the second.
cm_double_bishop_1.explanation: Two bishops on adjacent diagonals act like lasers, controlling every exit square.

cm_two_bishops_1.title: Two Bishops Corner Drive
cm_two_bishops_1.instruction: White to move. Begin netting the Black King into the corner.
hints: Form a wall of diagonals that cuts off half the board.
cm_two_bishops_1.explanation: With two bishops, place them side-by-side on adjacent diagonals to build an impenetrable barrier that pushes the enemy king to the rim.

cm_two_bishops_2.title: Delivering Two Bishops Mate
cm_two_bishops_2.instruction: White to move. Deliver checkmate with the two bishops.
hints: Cut off the king's exit step by step.
cm_two_bishops_2.explanation: Step-by-step diagonal control leaves the lone king with nowhere to flee.

cm_kb_1.title: Driving King to the Right Corner
cm_kb_1.instruction: White has a light-squared bishop. To mate Black, Black's king must be driven to a light-squared corner (h1 or a8). Find the restricting move.
hints: Place the bishop on the long diagonal to cut off escape toward the center.
cm_kb_1.explanation: In Knight and Bishop checkmate, you can ONLY checkmate in the corner of the same color as your bishop. Use the W-maneuver to herd the king there.

cm_kb_2.title: Knight & Bishop Finishing Net
cm_kb_2.instruction: White to move. Deliver checkmate in 2 moves in the light-squared corner.
hints: Check on the diagonal first to force the king into the corner.
cm_kb_2.explanation: The bishop and knight coordinate: the knight covers dark squares while the bishop covers light squares.

tac_pin_1.title: The Absolute Pin
tac_pin_1.instruction: White to move. Pin Black's queen to the king or exploit Black's pinned pieces.
hints: Kick the pinning bishop on b4.
tac_pin_1.explanation: An absolute pin occurs when a piece cannot legally move because it exposes the king to check.

tac_pin_2.title: Pinning the Queen
tac_pin_2.instruction: White to move. Win Black's Queen with an absolute pin.
hints: Capture the pinned queen on e7!
tac_pin_2.explanation: A pinned piece cannot run away. Here the queen is pinned to the king along the e-file.

tac_pin_3.title: Relative Pin on the Knight
tac_pin_3.instruction: White to move. Relieve tension by challenging Black's pinned pieces.
hints: Liquidate the central knight before Black can exploit the pin.
tac_pin_3.explanation: In a relative pin, moving the piece is legal but loses higher material (like a queen or rook).

tac_pin_4.title: Cross-Pin Winning Material
tac_pin_4.instruction: White to move. Invade the open c-file to pin down Black's pieces.
hints: Attack the d7 bishop from the 7th rank.
tac_pin_4.explanation: Piling pressure on pinned pieces paralyzes the enemy position.

tac_skewer_1.title: The Classical Skewer
tac_skewer_1.instruction: White to move. Skewer the enemy king and queen.
hints: The king and queen are aligned on the same file.
tac_skewer_1.explanation: A skewer is an attack on two pieces in a line where the more valuable piece is in front and must move, exposing the piece behind it.

tac_skewer_2.title: Bishop Diagonal Skewer
tac_skewer_2.instruction: White to move. Skewer the enemy King to win the Rook on f3.
hints: Find a diagonal that lines up Black's King and Rook.
tac_skewer_2.explanation: Bishops are deadly skewer weapons across long, open diagonals.

tac_skewer_3.title: Rook Endgame Skewer
tac_skewer_3.instruction: White to move. Secure the open rank advantage.
hints: Swing the rook to the 8th rank to prepare a rear skewer.
tac_skewer_3.explanation: Rooks can skewer defending kings along back ranks and open files.

tac_fork_1.title: Knight Royal Fork
tac_fork_1.instruction: White to move. Fork Black's King, Queen, and Rook with one devastating leap!
hints: Look for the knight jump that checks the king while simultaneously attacking the queen.
tac_fork_1.explanation: A knight fork attacks two or more pieces simultaneously. Because knights jump over pieces, they cannot be blocked.

tac_fork_2.title: Pawn Fork
tac_fork_2.instruction: White to move. Strike the center with a pawn fork.
hints: Eliminate the knight on e4, opening the d-file.
tac_fork_2.explanation: Pawns are the cheapest pieces, making pawn forks nearly impossible to neutralize without material loss.

tac_fork_3.title: Queen Double Attack
tac_fork_3.instruction: Black to move. Attack two unprotected pieces simultaneously.
hints: Check White's king while targeting the knight.
tac_fork_3.explanation: The queen's multidirectional movement makes it the ultimate double-attack piece.

tac_fork_4.title: Central Outpost Fork
tac_fork_4.instruction: White to move. Seize the center with a tactical pawn advance.
hints: Break open the center with e4.
tac_fork_4.explanation: Central pawn advances create multi-piece attacking opportunities.

tac_disc_1.title: Discovered Check Winning the Queen
tac_disc_1.instruction: White to move. Discover a check on Black's King while snatching the Queen!
hints: Move the queen to create a battery along the e-file.
tac_disc_1.explanation: A discovered attack happens when moving one piece reveals an attack from another piece hiding behind it.

tac_disc_2.title: Knight Leap Discovery
tac_disc_2.instruction: White to move. Unleash a tactical breakthrough.
hints: Sacrifice the bishop on h7 to expose Black's king.
tac_disc_2.explanation: Sacrifices that uncover lines for other attackers shatter enemy king safety.

tac_disc_3.title: Rook Battery Discovery
tac_disc_3.instruction: White to move. Exploit Black's loose rook on d8.
hints: Cash in immediately on the unprotected back rank.
tac_disc_3.explanation: Controlling the open file allows devastating exchanges that leave no response.

tac_dcheck_1.title: Unstoppable Double Check
tac_dcheck_1.instruction: White to move. Invade with a forcing check.
hints: The knight leap lands with decisive tempo.
tac_dcheck_1.explanation: Double check is the most lethal tactic in chess because neither checking piece can be captured, and the check cannot be blocked—the king MUST move.

tac_dcheck_2.title: King Hunt via Double Check
tac_dcheck_2.instruction: White to move. Double check the King into submission.
hints: Unmask the bishop check while jumping the knight.
tac_dcheck_2.explanation: Double checks allow attackers to leap freely into the line of fire since the king cannot capture both attackers.

tac_overload_1.title: The Overworked Defender
tac_overload_1.instruction: White to move. Black's e8 rook is overworked defending against back-rank mate and the file.
hints: Distract the king with a sacrifice on f7.
tac_overload_1.explanation: An overloaded piece is tasked with defending two different squares or pieces. Attack one, and the defense of the other collapses.

tac_overload_2.title: Queen Overload Strike
tac_overload_2.instruction: White to move. Win the c-file exchange.
hints: Deliver the back-rank blow immediately.
tac_overload_2.explanation: When an overworked piece cannot cover both duties, simplify directly into a winning endgame.

tac_zwischen_1.title: The Intermediate Check
tac_zwischen_1.instruction: White to move. Instead of recapturing, throw in an in-between check with the bishop.
hints: Disrupt Black's expected move order with a surprise check.
tac_zwischen_1.explanation: A Zwischenzug (in-between move) completely flips an expected sequence of trades by inserting a tempo-gaining threat.

tac_zwischen_2.title: Intermediate Counter-Threat
tac_zwischen_2.instruction: White to move. Seize the 7th rank with intermediate force.
hints: Attack before playing passive consolidation.
tac_zwischen_2.explanation: Interjecting active threats keeps the initiative on your side.

tac_xray_1.title: X-Ray Defense through Enemy Rook
tac_xray_1.instruction: White to move. Centralize rooks with x-ray power.
hints: Land on the 7th rank where your rook attacks through Black's defenders.
tac_xray_1.explanation: X-Ray attacks protect or attack squares through an intervening enemy piece along a file, rank, or diagonal.

tac_xray_2.title: Bishop X-Ray Snatch
tac_xray_2.instruction: White to move. Maintain diagonal mastery.
hints: Shield the 1st rank while keeping sight of Black's queenside.
tac_xray_2.explanation: Long-range pieces dominate by exerting pressure through lines of tension.

adv_zug_1.title: Pawn Endgame Zugzwang
adv_zug_1.instruction: White to move. Find the waiting move that puts Black in Zugzwang.
hints: Step back directly in front of the pawn to retain opposition.
adv_zug_1.explanation: Zugzwang means 'compulsion to move'. In chess, you cannot pass your turn—when every move loses, Zugzwang decides the game.

adv_zug_2.title: Minor Piece Zugzwang
adv_zug_2.instruction: White to move. Waste a tempo to force Black's king backward.
hints: Slide the bishop along the diagonal without changing its control.
adv_zug_2.explanation: Triangulation and tempo moves force the defender into unfavorable positions.

adv_interfere_1.title: Cutting Off Queen Defense
adv_interfere_1.instruction: White to move. Execute the back-rank liquidation.
hints: Capture the trapped rook with check!
adv_interfere_1.explanation: Interference cuts the line of communication between two defending enemy pieces, leaving one or both defenseless.

adv_interfere_2.title: Knight Wedge Interference
adv_interfere_2.instruction: White to move. Post a knight on the central outpost.
hints: Block Black's rook on the a-file while challenging the light-squared bishop.
adv_interfere_2.explanation: Planting a piece on the intersection of two enemy defensive lines causes instant tactical collapse.

adv_greekgift_1.title: The Classical Bxh7+ Sacrifice
adv_greekgift_1.instruction: White to move. Black has castled and lacks a defensive knight on f6. Strike at h7!
hints: Sacrifice the bishop on h7 with check, follow up with Ng5+ and Qh5.
adv_greekgift_1.explanation: The Greek Gift sacrifice (Bxh7+) rips open the enemy king's shelter when there is no defending knight on f6 to guard h7 and g5.

adv_greekgift_2.title: Greek Gift King Chase
adv_greekgift_2.instruction: White to move. Launch the kingside assault.
hints: Shatter the kingside pawn structure.
adv_greekgift_2.explanation: Once the h-pawn falls, White's queen and knight quickly swarm the exposed enemy king.

adv_deflect_1.title: Deflecting the Back-Rank Guard
adv_deflect_1.instruction: White to move. Attack the c8 rook while threatening mate.
hints: Deflect the rook away from the c-file.
adv_deflect_1.explanation: Deflection lures or forces an enemy piece away from an essential defensive duty.

adv_deflect_2.title: Deflection Bishop Sacrifice
adv_deflect_2.instruction: White to move. Snatch the exchange on f8.
hints: Trade off Black's key defender.
adv_deflect_2.explanation: Removing defenders by force leaves remaining enemy pieces disorganized.

adv_deflect_3.title: Queen Deflection Strike
adv_deflect_3.instruction: White to move. Centralize with decisive pressure.
hints: Deflect Black's attention to their vulnerable back rank.

adv_attract_1.title: King Decoy Sacrifice
adv_attract_1.instruction: White to move. Decoy Black's rook into a fatal pin.
hints: Trade rooks on the back rank.
adv_attract_1.explanation: Attraction lures an enemy piece (especially the king or queen) onto a fatal square where a fork, pin, or checkmate awaits.

adv_attract_2.title: Attracting the King to a Fork
adv_attract_2.instruction: White to move. Infiltrate the open file.
hints: Invade the 7th rank.
adv_attract_2.explanation: Placing pieces on the 7th rank restricts the king's movement.

adv_underprom_1.title: Underpromotion to Knight with Check
adv_underprom_1.instruction: White to move. Promote the pawn, but promoting to a queen might allow stalemate or miss a fork. Promote to Knight!
hints: Underpromote to Knight to give check and fork!
adv_underprom_1.explanation: Underpromotion to a Knight gives an unexpected check or fork, while promoting to a Rook or Bishop avoids accidental stalemate.

adv_underprom_2.title: Avoiding Stalemate with Rook Underpromotion
adv_underprom_2.instruction: White to move. If White promotes to Queen, it's instant STALEMATE! Promote to Rook instead!
hints: Promote to Rook to deliver checkmate without stalemate.
adv_underprom_2.explanation: A queen would control too many squares, causing a draw. A rook delivers clean checkmate.

adv_desperado_1.title: The Doomed Knight
adv_desperado_1.instruction: White to move. Play aggressively before conceding pieces.
hints: Force the exchange on your terms.
adv_desperado_1.explanation: A desperado piece is already doomed or captured; before dying, it takes as much enemy material with it as possible.

adv_desperado_2.title: Desperado Pawn Strike
adv_desperado_2.instruction: White to move. Trade off into a won endgame.
hints: Cash in the rook on the back rank.
adv_desperado_2.explanation: Trading doomed pieces preserves your structural advantage.

adv_ccheck_1.title: Parrying with Check
adv_ccheck_1.instruction: White to move. Pin Black's rook along the e-file.
hints: Trade rooks directly to nullify Black's threats.
adv_ccheck_1.explanation: A counter-check responds to a check by interposing a piece that delivers check to the opponent's king at the exact same moment!

adv_ccheck_2.title: Cross-Pin Counter Check
adv_ccheck_2.instruction: White to move. Black just played Bb4+ check! Block the check and attack Black's bishop!
hints: Interpose the bishop on d2.
adv_ccheck_2.explanation: Blocking checks with active developing pieces turns defense into attack.

adv_undermine_1.title: Destroying the Central Pawn Anchor
adv_undermine_1.instruction: White to move. Strike Black's d5 anchor with the c-pawn lever.
hints: Exchange on d5 to undermine Black's pawn chain.
adv_undermine_1.explanation: Undermining attacks the root of an enemy pawn chain or defensive formation to bring down the whole structure.

adv_undermine_2.title: Removing the Guardian
adv_undermine_2.instruction: White to move. Eliminate the d5 knight defending Black's center.
hints: Capture on d5.
adv_undermine_2.explanation: Removing the key defender leaves the adjacent pieces undefended.

adv_clear_1.title: Diagonal Clearance
adv_clear_1.instruction: White to move. Prepare kingside development.
hints: Develop the bishop to unpin the c3 knight.
adv_clear_1.explanation: A clearance sacrifice vacates a critical square, file, or diagonal for a more decisive attacking piece to use.

adv_clear_2.title: Clearance for the Queen
adv_clear_2.instruction: White to move. Lift the queen into the attack.
hints: Step the queen out to h5 threatening mate on h7.
adv_clear_2.explanation: Clearing the path for queen entry creates lethal double threats.

end_key_1.title: King in Front of Pawn
end_key_1.instruction: White to move. Maintain king position in front of your pawn.
hints: Do not push the pawn immediately! Place the king first.
end_key_1.explanation: In King and Pawn endings, the king must march ahead of the pawn to secure key squares and escort the pawn to queen.

end_key_2.title: Seizing the Critical Square
end_key_2.instruction: White to move. Step forward to claim key squares.
hints: Keep the king ahead of the d3 pawn.
end_key_2.explanation: If your king controls the key squares in front of your pawn, promotion is mathematically guaranteed.

end_key_3.title: Escorting the Queen
end_key_3.instruction: White to move. Promote to Queen!
hints: Push the pawn to the 8th rank.
end_key_3.explanation: With the defending king out of range, the pawn promotes effortlessly.

end_opp_1.title: Direct Vertical Opposition
end_opp_1.instruction: White to move. Step into direct opposition.
hints: Move such that an odd number of squares separates the kings.
end_opp_1.explanation: Having the opposition means your opponent must step aside and allow your king to infiltrate.

end_opp_2.title: Shouldering the Opponent
end_opp_2.instruction: White to move. Shoulder Black's king away from the center.
hints: Take the direct opposition on d3.
end_opp_2.explanation: Shouldering uses your king's body to block the enemy king from reaching defensive squares.

end_pawn7_1.title: Queen vs 7th-Rank Rook Pawn Draw
end_pawn7_1.instruction: White to move. Promote the pawn and finish the game.
hints: Promote to Queen on h8!
end_pawn7_1.explanation: A rook pawn or bishop pawn on the 7th rank can draw against a queen because the defending king hides in the corner with stalemate threats.

end_pawn7_2.title: Driving Defending King In Front
end_pawn7_2.instruction: White to move. King is safe on h1.
hints: Wait on h2.
end_pawn7_2.explanation: When defending against a 7th rank pawn, forcing the king in front of its own pawn gains vital tempos.

end_lucena_1.title: The Lucena Position (Building a Bridge)
end_lucena_1.instruction: White to move. The cornerstone winning technique in rook endgames! Cut off Black's king.
hints: Lift the rook to the 4th rank (Rc4). This builds the bridge on b4 against Black's checks!
end_lucena_1.explanation: The Lucena Position is the most important position in rook endgames: lifting the rook to the 4th rank allows White to block vertical checks and queen the pawn.

end_philidor_1.title: The Philidor Defense (3rd Rank Cut)
end_philidor_1.instruction: White to move. Keep Black's king cut off.
hints: Anchor the rook on the 7th rank to paralyze the enemy king.
end_philidor_1.explanation: The Philidor position is the fundamental drawing method in rook endgames: keep your rook on the 3rd rank until the pawn pushes, then swing to the back rank for rear checks.

end_rook_cut_1.title: Cutting the King Along the File
end_rook_cut_1.instruction: White to move. Cut Black's king off from the kingside.
hints: Slide the rook to h4 to keep the king isolated on the queenside.
end_rook_cut_1.explanation: Cutting the enemy king off along a file renders it useless for stopping your advancing pawns.

end_rook_active_1.title: Active Rook Defense
end_rook_active_1.instruction: White to move. An active rook is worth more than a passive pawn.
hints: Give check and seek the open back rank.
end_rook_active_1.explanation: In rook endings, passive rooks lose. Always seek active positions and rear checks.

end_tarrasch_rule_1.title: Tarrasch's Rule (Rook Behind the Passed Pawn)
end_tarrasch_rule_1.instruction: White to move. Protect your passed pawn from behind.
hints: Keep the rook behind the pawn so its power expands as the pawn advances.
end_tarrasch_rule_1.explanation: Tarrasch's Rule: Rooks belong BEHIND passed pawns—both your own (to support them) and the opponent's (to arrest them).

end_passer_race_1.title: The Passed Pawn Race
end_passer_race_1.instruction: White to move. Surround the pawn before it can queen.
hints: Bring the king to c2 to capture the b2 pawn.
end_passer_race_1.explanation: When the enemy rook cannot support its pawn, marching the king directly to the pawn wins it.

mid_outpost_1.title: The Dominant d5 Outpost
mid_outpost_1.instruction: White to move. Establish a powerful central presence.
hints: Open lines for piece expansion.
mid_outpost_1.explanation: An outpost is a central square protected by a pawn that cannot be attacked by enemy pawns. Knights on outposts are monsters.

mid_outpost_2.title: Octopus Knight on e5
mid_outpost_2.instruction: White to move. Leap into the dominant e5 outpost!
hints: Plant the knight on e5.
mid_outpost_2.explanation: Central outposts radiating power in eight directions are called 'Octopus Knights'.

mid_files_1.title: Seizing the Open c-file
mid_files_1.instruction: White to move. Infiltrate the 7th rank along the open c-file.
hints: Invade c7!
mid_files_1.explanation: Open files are highways for your rooks. The goal of controlling an open file is to reach the 7th rank ('Pigs on the Seventh').

mid_files_2.title: Doubling Rooks on Open File
mid_files_2.instruction: White to move. Double rooks on the c-file for unstoppable invasion.
hints: Land on c7 and back it up with Rec1.
mid_files_2.explanation: Doubled rooks on an open file compound pressure and force material concessions.

mid_lever_1.title: The c4 Pawn Lever
mid_lever_1.instruction: White to move. Blast open Black's solid pawn chain with the c4 pawn lever!
hints: Challenge d5 by pushing c2-c4.
mid_lever_1.explanation: A pawn lever is a pawn push that comes into contact with an enemy pawn to pry open files and shatter locked centers.

mid_lever_2.title: The e4 Break in Queen's Pawn
mid_lever_2.instruction: White to move. Prepare the central e4 breakthrough.
hints: Develop the bishop to d3 to support e4.
mid_lever_2.explanation: Central breaks dictate the tempo of the middlegame.

mid_kingsafety_1.title: Opposite-Side Castling Storm
mid_kingsafety_1.instruction: White to move. Advance kingside pawns to pry open Black's castled shelter.
hints: Launch the queenside pawn storm with b4!
mid_kingsafety_1.explanation: In opposite-side castling games, speed is everything. Pawn storms rip open lines to the enemy monarch.

mid_kingsafety_2.title: Weak Dark Square Infiltration
mid_kingsafety_2.instruction: White to move. Challenge Black's fianchetto pawn formation.
hints: Clarify the central pawn structure.
mid_kingsafety_2.explanation: Targeting holes in the enemy fianchetto setup exposes the king to decisive mating attacks.
